I do acknowledge the value of these "virtues". In fact, I am willing to commit my complete support for such values! But you must understand, sir, actual value must be quantifiable.
What does the audience like better? Courage or valor? Generosity or mercy? We don't need a just arbitrator when we already have the most reliable judge of our products — the market itself! Sir, a man of your years and experience should have seen the great upheavals when the index figures fluctuated and the lines leaped up and down the charts... Oh! You and your grandfather actually visited the old Terran General Chamber of Commerce...? Wonderful! Truly wonderful childhood memories! I'll just skip the things you already know. You should be well aware that everything we see is the result of our efforts in quantifying "virtues" into actual value that we can trade with.
Of course. Commerce is a field of knowledge exclusive to humanity. Oh, and I got something about that. Forget about the rancorous criticisms of our top economists and financial experts. I don't care if we're living on a sphere, on top of a pyramid, or a pillar. Makes no difference to us as long as the people living here are human. We never left ourselves. What I meant was that living at a new place didn't suddenly give us a new mind.
Those who wanted to keep moving describe this place as untamed and filled with dangers. But I see a land untouched and filled with potential! I can't emphasize enough the immensity of the profits we can reap by investing in this project. The Virtues-series equipment is but the smallest step in our great strategy... And I am not the only one who recognizes this opportunity. You'd be wise to keep that in mind.
Mr. Derriam, before they fill the entire place up with people and start putting price tags on all sorts of "virtues" ... I promise, every cent you invest via this contract will grant you incalculable wealth in the future.
Oh, that's right! Just sign right there... I knew I saw a keen-eyed investor who saw exactly where the killing can be made — Hold on. Got to take this call. Yes? Good. Have him wait in the VIP lounge.
— And that should wrap things up. Don't let me keep you here, sir.

-6052654399623495943:
The sun had yet to rise.
The warrior of the Coldpine Tribe was already awake. His hand held a short charcoal pen and the paper beneath it was barely larger than his palm.
Every space counted, for there was a lot that he wanted to write. He scratched the words carefully and read every word out loud. Though he tried to keep his voice low, the one next to him stirred. The woman opened her remaining eye, gave him a vicious kick and a cold rasp: "Quiet."
The warrior gave her a foolish smile, then started reciting his writings silently in his mind: "Dear Mamma, the ice has melted and we could see the green mosses. They feel good. They look lovely. I believe spring has arrived at your place. The river must be flowing beneath your treehouse and giving water to the plants in the garden. The fowls have probably returned to roost beneath the roof, fluttering into the house when you open the window so they can rest in your hand. Perhaps a day will come when I can fly home to you like the fowls, and stay by your side where spring is eternal, and..."
It was a word that his mother often spoke of. The warrior remembered it but forgot how it was shaped. Left with no choice, he stopped writing and gave the woman a look of resignation and a sincere need for help.
The woman's annoyed words did not hide an undertone of curiosity: "Why stop writing?"
"There's a word, but I can't shape it."
"And what is that word?"
"Sa-Sanctuary."
"You never learned it?"
"Mamma left me before she taught me the word."
"Ooooooh," the woman dragged it out as though frustrated. She then raised her hand and drew it in the air, a criss-crossing pattern of curved arcs and straight lines, like the mid-air trails left by a darting fowl.
The woman wrote out the word quickly at first. The warrior's tired eyes could barely keep track of her fingertip. She saw his knotted brows and chuckled, and then wrote the word out again.
Together, the warrior's charcoal pen, the woman's finger, the lines on the paper, and the shape in the air formed the word. It came together like a fowl making a slow landing on the ground.
The paper was now full of words. He gave a satisfied smile and then chucked it into the campfire. It crackled as it burned, and the firelight danced in the woman's eye before spluttering out at the corner of her gaze.
"You believe this would never reach her?"
The warrior nodded. The woman let out a sigh. There was a moment of silence before she suddenly spoke again. "What is your name, child?"
"Björn, of the Coldpines."
The woman reminisced as she voiced out her memories, one fragment at a time: "The Coldpine Tribe... Oh yes, I remember your Chieftain... A brave warrior, and very admirable. She honored the warrior's creed when she fell."
"I am fortunate, for I grew up with her," the warrior's face was flushed as he nodded at her with gratitude.
"May she return to Sami's side, a place of eternal spring, the..."
"The Sanctuary," the warrior said the word together with the woman as she smiled.
The sun had yet to rise, but the horns were trumpeting. The Aggeloi appeared at the horizon, marching towards the frontlines as a mighty host.
The Coldpine warrior was already on his feet. He took up the spear and carried the woman. Together with the soldiers, he turned to face the Aggeloid tide.
Behind them, the fires consumed the paper. Stray embers flew out of flickering tongues and floated to a faraway place.

-5866475591618458440:
Camille Arno, Seš'qa's Agaš'mekanaz (Keeper of Wisdom), sought a partnership with Endfield Industries in a personal capacity. Following a recommendation from the Endministrator, he currently holds a position within the Specialist Tech Division. 

Operator Camille's parents were members of the joint science expedition from Terra. He himself was born and raised in Seš'qa. However, due to the requirements of his job and his past experiences, Camille has lived outside the floating city for many years. 
Although Camille claims to be "hunting" a criminal kin, his extremely long yet blank curriculum vitae suggests that he has quietly swapped his roles of "hunter" and "prey". The entire corpus of his social relations, personal background ... or his "life", if we were to adopt a broader definition, has been completely destroyed across a period of several decades. 
When I picked this up in the discussion, Camille averted his gaze to the ceiling and stared at a blotch. He then broke the silence with a stream of metaphors and figures of speech. One of them, which I felt was most impressive, was how he described himself as a "pendulum working in vain". 
He went on and said there was a certain day when his time stopped ticking. 
When the conversation was over, I walked away with the most important lesson when engaging with this operator — If you wish to avoid the excessive task of emotional management, DO NOT talk about his sibling. 
— Martin Marvin Malen, Assistant, HR Division, Endfield Industries

Thank you for visiting my humble abode. Please, take a seat. Apologies for being unable to greet you on my two feet. Ah, just a fracture of the calf bones. I'll be out of the plaster next month. It's healing nicely and I don't think anything worse could happen. 
I'm more than happy to support your investigation. But really, this is just a minor issue of being bested by my betters, to put it simply... Oh yes, there's no personal grudges or disagreements between the two of us. I formally submitted my application to her and took part in the "trials" as agreed. Now, I'd never met Lady Azrila. However, it was an opportunity for joining the Order of Steel Oath and their legendary banners. If you've read anything about their crusading traditions, and if you're the type of person who wants to defend the homes of your people, no warrior would ever let this opportunity slip by. Pardon my insolence, but what actually makes you think this is an issue of personal grudges? 
...She didn't pass anyone? Not even that champion knight from the majors? Is that so? That's a little different from what I've been told. Regardless, I do not agree with your guesses. People can indeed communicate with each other by crossing their blades, and our blades did cross. Let me think... Oh, something small did happen afterwards. I hope it'll help you decide what really happened. 
Lady Azrila actually paid me a visit after the "trials". I sensed there was something on her mind, and I was concerned she felt guilty for not stopping her sword in time and accidentally hurting me. So that was what I asked, but she just smiled apologetically and countered with a question of her own: "Was there any time when you felt helpless?" 
Honestly, I felt helpless in more occasions than I could ever hope for. But given the circumstances and vibe of our conversation, I believe that we were not talking about the same thing. 
"The powerful enemy is before you, but you no longer had the strength to even swing your blade. Your comrades are slowly losing every hope of victory just to keep you alive... What would you do in this situation? Or rather, what would you let them do?" 
I have no idea why she asked me this question or what she hoped to get out of it. I just gave her my honest answer: "I would hate to admit this, but if I'm already a piece of dead weight, I might as well give my comrades another chance. We can't afford to suffer any defeats. The Civilization Band is right behind us." 
I was trying to join the Order of Steel Oath and it was natural for me to read about the stories from the frontlines. But ... she looked really conflicted after listening to my answer. "Nilla and Claire did exactly that," she said, "They all did... And this is why I cannot approve you." 
Blightery, that was the first time my brain ever overclocked itself. I had a feeling that she did not outright disagree with me. She seemed to be hesitating about other things... No. I don't really care about passing or failing her trials. I just want to help. It was during this time that Lady Azrila seemed as though she was ... in need of serious help. 
So, I did my best to think about all sorts of possibilities and acted as though I know what actually happened. I told her, "If you're seeking revenge on an enemy, just remember that nobody wants their friend to die trying to avenge them." 
...Yeah, even I felt it was a dumb thing to say and I immediately regretted my words. Then we said absolutely nothing for about five minutes or so. But Lady Azrila was actually really friendly. She forced herself to smile and comforted me by praising my combat skills. She even told me I could seek the others out and try again after my wounds heal. 
And after that, we talked a little bit more before she left... Oh, before I forget, she also asked me plenty of things about you. Since you're here specifically to ask me all these questions, does that mean she's going to stay at Endfield Industries for a while? 

(NOTES: This is followed by friendly banter that does not require specific review. Also, we advise getting the logistics operators ready. Operator Ember may need to receive an ordinary visitor next month.)

-5671734292380321703:
Somewhere in the wildlands, a convoy of heavy caravans switched off their engines and parked before the roadblock. The wind-stirred dust raked against the windows as the dull booms of explosions and things hitting the ground reverberated.
A young trucker lowered the window and poked his head out. "Blasted weather. Looks like it's gonna rain again! And do we have more buggerloids up ahead? This is our third encounter this month!"
An older trucker got out of the cab. The Originium device of his caravan was already attempting to clean the windshield of the dust. "The redistribution post has dispatched an emergency team. See that engineering vehicle? The crew is already clearing the rubble off the road."
"Eh, mate. You look like a real veteran. Seen any special buggers?" the young trucker asked curiously.
The old man lit a cigarette: "Saw one at a nearby outpost ten years ago. Blasted buggerloid was bigger than a caravan. I also witnessed a fellow trucker scampering into the cab."
"Did he make it?"
"Well, that oversized bugger followed but couldn't hold its grip. Rolled off with the caravan container and got crushed by fifty tons of raw Originium ore."
"Sounds like a really stupid bugger. Man, that trucker got super lucky. People told me there were rocky-crawlies all over this place back then."
"It was way worse back then," the old trucker blew a smoke ring into the air. "This highway didn't exist, and there were no RD posts nor support teams from the TGCC. It was a time when local town and villages, no matter the size, would fight each other or breakers over tinned provisions."
That got the young trucker interested. Half of his body was almost out of his cab. "Fighting breaker clans over a few tins? Dayyum. All I see are just crafters selling their wares and stuff nowadays. I even see people from Kjersch."
"That was how we founded the Chamber of Commerce. The entire venture started with a dozen or so very experienced truckers. My mentor was amongst the Chamber Founders," the old trucker smiled. "See that Endfield installation? It ran out of food ten years ago. We took the risk, forced our way through breaker turf, and delivered the food. That was my first time behind a caravan wheel."
"I bet they were super grateful about the food."
"Not really. They mopped the floor with a band of breakers who tried to raid them. The Endfielders looted the breakers' rations and that kept them going for a while."

The sound of explosions got closer and the rubble began cascading off the slopes of the hill in the far distance. The truckers waited patiently for passage.
"The RD post kept talking about ... 'business conformance'," the young trucker got back into his cab and took out a huge bar of chocolate. He tore off a piece and threw it at another trucker who waited by his caravan. "Route reviews are okay, just a tiny waste of time. But now they're even slapping a uniform price on Origo-fueling, and the price is friggin' ex. These guys are siphoning our T-Creds."
Another trucker taking a walk overheard the conversation and decided to join in. "Say what you want, but things would be so much better if we didn't have to pay TGCC its cut."
"Then who's gonna mint the T-Creds? Who's gonna take care of freelancing truckers like us?" the veteran trucker smiled as he puffed another smoke ring.
"Oh?"
"And forget about that Extra Crispy Drumsticks from Caravan Express, or decently priced fueling stops when the TGCC disappears."
"I...," the young trucker was at a loss of words. He finally shook his hands and returned to his cabin. "Meh. He can't even take a joke about the cartel."

They heard another explosion, this time closer than before.
"The TGCC is all about big business nowadays..." the trucker added after his momentary hesitation. "Heard about some company trying to monopolize Origo-fuel supplies..."
The veteran trucker looked at the smoke in the distance.
"Monopolies... The last one who ignored the Accord and tried to do that got a generous serving of jail time, courtesy of the TGCC joint session. Speaking of which, trading of key resources will always be controlled, but they're doing it for the Northern Front. I made plenty of deliveries to that place. Those trips were really hairy."
"Oh, the North, right? I actually squished a buggerloid with my truck."

A few workers at the front of the caravan suddenly carried the roadblock away. A raspy noise blared out of the Originium radios: "Road section cleared. Roll along and keep your distance."
"You're going to Valley IV, right? I guess this is where we part ways," the young trucker roared as loud as he could.
"Are you tired of me already? I'm heading to Wuling too!" the old trucker strapped into his seat and checked his rearview mirror. "We're far from parting ways."
"Da hell, old boy? Are you following me or something?"
"You take me as a stalker? I'm gonna load up on food at Wuling, drop them at Valley IV, get some Originium ore for Kjersch, and then haul a container full of craftwork to La Fantoma."
The truckers continued their crude banter, started their engines, and got back into the never-ending caravans.

DOCUMENT: Uncle Pan the Everchenjing 
Uncle Pan the Everchenjing lives in Wuling and hes like the most warmest person i've ever seen. Hes black and white and his eyes look like grapes. His ears look like gold yuanbao and he looks very cool with his sunglasses. 
Uncle Pan can transform and he's got all sorts of clothes like a big white shef apron or crew overalls. Sometimes he also wears a yellow plastic hat. Uncle Pan also has a hot pot shop and tolds us that we can have meals at his place if we miss home and if we got tired of hot pot he will make other delishus stuff like mantow buns, flashy fryd kidnees, or sweet sour fins. The best food made by Uncle Pan is the veeneger bokk choy and refryd meat and he wants to make them the chefs speshow. 
But sometimes Uncle Pan plays pranks on us. He puts spisy saos in my lunch box but tells me its magic jam so i share the magic jam with my frenz and everyone got sosejj lips. 
Uncle Pan takes care of the kids and he also helps other people. He can fix power meeters, do plumming and pipes, chop the bamboos. Cos Uncle Pan is so helpful to everyone, everyone also wants to help Uncle Pan. But Uncle Pan is reely powerfol and theres nothing we can help him with, so we gave him delishus fruits and sweets... and the landlord lowerd his hot pot shop rent. Peepo say that Uncle Pan is homeless cos his home eksploddeded so he has to spend money to liv in a frenz home. 

One day i ask Uncle Pan why he made no money after working for many years. He told me he spent all the money on food but later i lerned that he spent all the money on the kids... 
— Chen Qianyu 

His passion and friendliness are infectious. People often start spilling their beans and sharing their stories within minutes after meeting him. But the reverse does not apply. Operator Da Pan rarely talks about his own story. Nevertheless, many still regard him as the "friendly HAS tianshi who really knows how to cook". A painful past may be a burden to bear. Being a listener with few words makes him a decent friend. However, being secretive and keeping to oneself are rarely good things. 
My other concern is that after Da Pan arrived at Dijiang, many of our operators (and our Endministrator as well) began putting on significant amounts of weight... 
— Perlica

DOCUMENT: Combat Adaptation Test Records (ID: L-067) 
CANDIDATE: Laevatain (reconvener) 
MONITOR: Krad (Endfield Security Professional) 
OS: S7 Combat Simulation System 
CONTENTS: Mass suppression and precision strikes 
DURATION: 3 minutes 42 seconds 
RESULTS: Pass (conditional) 

TEST SUMMARY 
At the 7th second of Phase 1, Operator Laevatain summons a giant flaming blade with one hand (no equipment ID identified; said blade is likely created by Laevatain's Originium Arts) and charges directly into the center of the simulated enemy group before verbal instructions were given nor confirmed. 
At the 31st second, thermal readings exceeded simulation environment monitoring thresholds. System automatically activates anti-heat measures. Security Professional Krad requests to stop the test but Operator Laevatain denies the request. 
At the 1-minute and 24-second mark, Operator Laevatain had destroyed all enemy units and assumed a standing pose in the center of the simulation area, while adjusting her breathing after a high-intensity burst of activities. 
Combat resumed after 38 seconds to initiate Phase 2. Test item "Stationery Suppression" was initiated. The operator's performance was far more extreme than Phase 1 and the entire test was completed after 1 minute and 40 seconds. 

BEHAVIORAL SUMMARY 
Combat style is highly aggressive and prioritizes breaking the stalemate with overwhelming force. 
Prefers seizing combat initiative instead of focusing on tactical coordination. Willingness to support teamwork is unstable. 
Weapon efficacy is significantly improved at emotional thresholds. Effects include spreading fire, localized scorch marks, and signal interference. 

TEST REVIEW 
She is incredibly powerful but has yet to build up the mental fortitude to master it. She does not enjoy destruction, but uses combat as a means to vent her emotions and prove her existence. She must learn how to restrain herself and bring that instability under control — master the fire, but don't become the fire. If she loses her connection to medic or support operators in the team, no one would be able to save her. 
— Evaluations by Krad, Security Professional 

I don't think you gave me this test to see if I can still fight. You wanted to know if I would "lose control", right? Don't worry ... I know exactly what I'm doing. 
— Comments from Operator Laevatain 

NOTE: New thermal insulation must be installed in the combat testing area. If there is another test, also prepare 3 servings of Coolant Beverages. 

DOCUMENT: Post-Operational Summary (ID: SU-58R-TR) 
During this combat operation, Operator Laevatain charged into the enemy on her own accords at the initial stages of battle, and did not respond to tactical calls from her team. Her actions temporarily severed communications, disrupted the chain of command, and caused momentary panic amongst team members. Fortunately, the team did not suffer any casualties. 
When the operation ended, analyses of residual energy traces and tactical dataloggers confirmed that Operator Laevatain successfully diverted the focus of enemy fire toward herself with these means: deliberate exposure of her own position and continuous emission of super hot flames that disrupt enemy defenses. In other words, she used herself as a lure to create a tactical breach and allowed our attacking operators to exploit the opening and achieve our tactical objectives. 
Upon concluding the operation, Operator Laevatain sat on a cooled fragment of molten rock. Burn marks in the vicinity suggested that this area was subjected to extremely intensive strikes. Laevatain said nothing as we surveyed the battlefield. After ascertaining that all other operators were well, she softly said, "Good."

I've never really trusted my memory, and I don't keep a diary. 
But when I got back to my place at the Asphalt Roundabout and took out that album with Miss Liino's signature on it, all the happy memories from that day came rushing back. I just had to write this down. 

I've never been to La Fantoma before this fan meeting. Even though I booked my hotel a month in advance, I still got lost. Thankfully, a kind Feline helped me find my way. A lot of the guests there were probably fans like me. The front desk noticed my Liino plushie on my bag, told me the fastest route to the venue, and even suggested a nearby café. 
"It's the one Miss Liino mentioned in her interview! You might wanna try their signature drink." 
The next day, when I arrived at the venue, almost everyone was holding a cup of that café's signature drink. I had already bought one too, so I just quietly blended in. No one knew I had never actually watched a single Liino interview. 
Everyone around me looked so young and so clearly devoted. Compared to them, I really was just an ordinary fan. I only heard a few of Miss Liino's songs and liked her right away. Honestly, I never really cared about idols before her, and I had never been to a fan meeting before this. Everything about that day felt strange ... a little mysterious, and exciting in a way I can't really explain. 
When Miss Liino took the gift I nervously held out to her, said my name so warmly, and gently squeezed my hand, she said: 
"Twinkle-twinkle! I remember you! At the Asphalt Roundabout bus station, you helped Liino get her travel pass, didn't you?" 
I just nodded, speechless. Every line I'd practiced vanished. In the end, I just blurted a clumsy thank-you — 
"Thank you... I'm glad I could help..." 
I also wanted to tell her how much I loved that song she made up on the spot that day. But I couldn't get the words out. 
Yet somehow, she seemed to hear them anyway. She picked up the thread so naturally. 
"You still remember that song? It's gonna be in my next album! If you like it so much, you should come to Liino's concert next month. Liino will sing the full version live!" 
Then she placed the already-signed album into my hands, smiled, and said: 
"I hope I'll see you there, Evelyn!" 

Looking back, everything felt like a dream. 
I think I finally understand how those super passionate fans feel. When you're looking at someone that shines that brightly, it's impossible not to think ... "I wish I could see her again." 
I really, really hope I'll get to see Liino again someday. La Fantoma, New Wrankwood, Simonch, or even somewhere way farther away, I'd go without hesitation. 
I really would. 

— "A Fan Meeting I'll Never Forget" by a Bus Station Clerk Who Traveled Alone to Valley IV for Liino

Other operators aboard the Dijiang often say that Supervisor Perlica seems to possess a kind of magical quality. As long as she's around, any problem finds its solution. 
So when I learned that I'd have the privilege of studying alongside her, I was so excited I couldn't sleep. But reality hit me hard. Unable to keep up with her intense workload and exacting standards, I seriously considered quitting along the way … yet I couldn't bring myself to give up such a precious opportunity. 
With the expected awakening of the Endministrator just around the corner, everyone is on edge—even Supervisor Perlica is no exception. Despite her schedule being completely packed, she still manages to squeeze in meetings with senior members from every department to ensure everything goes off without a hitch. 
But after each of those impromptu private meetings, she always comes out looking uneasy. Could it be that there are things even she can't handle? I can't help but blame myself for not being able to do more to help. 
She noticed how lost I felt and took the initiative to comfort me, even sharing some strangely flavored fin meatballs I'd never seen before. The taste was so strong it brought tears to my eyes, yet Supervisor Perlica just watched me with a satisfied smile … That day's worries were washed away along with my tears. 
In that moment, I suddenly realized that Supervisor Perlica … truly does have that kind of magic. 
—From the work log of a trainee operator, who is still applying for the opportunity to continue her apprenticeship under Supervisor Perlica. 

[Record That Has Not Been Successfully Deleted] 
"She went to see you too, didn't she, Krad? Asking how to get along with the Endministrator she cares about so much, right?" 
"Wouldn't expect anything less from Intel. You're not even on the Dijiang and you're still this well-informed. When she rushed into the training room to find me, I thought something had gone wrong. But then she asked me that dead seriously. Totally took me by surprise." 
"Guess I've gotten so used to her being the Supervisor that I almost forgot she isn't actually invincible. But I do love that awkward tone she takes when she messages me. Still just as adorable as when we were kids."

[Graduation Speech] 
"Hmmm... Greetings, everyone. I am Zhuang Fangyi from the Class of ██. It is truly an honor to stand here today on behalf of my fellow graduates. 
"I'm the youngest amongst you. Even fellow students who just enrolled are two years ahead of me. So I'd like to begin by thanking everyone for your care and support throughout these years. 
"Thank you for helping me reach the top shelves when I couldn't. Thank you for always saving me a front-row seat for the lectures. Thank you for holding back your frustration even when experiments stalled... 
"Most of all, although everyone spoiled me with loving exceptions usually reserved to a younger sibling, none of my ideas or suggestions were ever brushed off as childish. I skipped many years in school and lost the chance to befriend peers of my age. But in return, I gained invaluable friendships with those older than me. I missed out on one kind of companionship, but received guidance, mentorship, and trust from another. 
"Now, my next step is to continue my studies at the Hongshan Academy of Sciences. The colleagues I meet there are likely to be even more experienced... I also hope to learn from them and build new friendships..." 

[Eulogy] 
"I am keenly aware that many among you are far more suited than I to stand here today and deliver this eulogy for those we have lost. In the presence of parents, sons and daughters, lifelong companions, and loved ones ... I am but a mere youth. 
"I was the youngest member at the Science Station. The reason I could convey our longing on behalf of everyone is a result of your patience, guidance, and care... 
"I have made a journey blessed with support from all sides. I often asked my experienced peers how I might repay the trust and sincerity they showed me. They would always smile and tell me that doing my work and honoring the expectations placed upon me were the best means of repayment. 
"Though they are no longer with us, the trust they invested in me has not waned, nor has their faith in the Xiranite project. I understand that this is the moment to repay them in full... 
"And faithfully I shall bear those hopes and expectations upon my shoulders." 

Orientation Speech 
"Greetings, everyone. It is a great honor to welcome you to Wuling, where you have chosen to commit your most beautiful years to the laboratories, to this place, and to the forefront of our fight against the Blight and the Rift. 
"I know many of you chose Wuling because your parents and elders who sacrificed everything for the Science Station... Seeing your young, eager faces brings back memories — I sat where you are seated right now, and listened to your parents and elders who led me onto this path. 
"I once thought their greatest gift to me was the scientific achievements they had spent their lives creating. Now I realize the gift includes you who arrived at Wuling — who answered their call to follow their footsteps. 
"I once believed that the best way to honor their memories was to stay on that path and reach, without hesitation, the ideal future they dreamed of. Now I understand that I must also lead those who follow, to guide them onto that path and help them envision the future... 
"Thank you. 
"Thank you for choosing to walk this path with me." 

Recording: New Operator Welcome Party 
"Am I tipsy already? Maybe a bit... But this isn't right. I only had a little.. 
"Is this the ninth? Hmm ... maybe it's a bit too much. 
"You know, the last time I felt this happy was when I first arrived at the Science Station. They threw me a welcome party too. 
"I was very young back then so I only had juice. But I felt tipsy just the same, watching them toast cup after cup and laugh without worry. The mood was perfect. 
"Today ... feels just like that again. The future is laid out before me, waiting for me to step forward. 
"What more is there to say? Nothing... Just being happy is enough."

You're still torturing me. 
I know it very well. This is my 1299th attempt to forget everything about you and your seductions, but I failed... We have been so close, and kept each other company for so long. How could I ever cast these memories aside...? 
Oh beloved left hand of mine. 
A year has passed since I had to amputate you for getting Blighted in the material science experiment. But I can still feel your existence. I can still feel your feedback whenever I stretch or curl the absent fingers or wave the bygone palm. The physician called it phantom pain and a common ailment. All I needed was to set my mind to rest, and maybe accept a few treatment courses and therapy sessions. But I know a quack when I see one. I know their kind well. 
We were only separated and I have not lost you. That is certain. I know where you are, although I am temporarily unable to reach your side. 
You are in the Ætherside. 
...... 
Ætherside, my love. The greatest source of trouble that we have faced together, back when we were still students and after we joined the Portable Æthertech Labs. The Ætherside has always been influencing our lives. Is there anyone else who knows more about the Ætherside than us? Probably not... Wait, no... I think they do exist, the Endfielders ... those working in the best labs of the TGCC and UWST ... and the strange ones who roam the wilderness but have a knack for it. They also have great knowledge for the Ætherside too. 
This is why I am confused, dear. My inability to find you made me realize that I hardly know anything about the Ætherside. Nothing living should exist there. I shouldn't be feeling you at all, but the gentle sensations emanating from the stump where you were severed felt so clear and real. Part of my mind is fighting another. The conclusion has caused the corpus of my knowledge, one that I have meticulously constructed over the years, to utterly collapse. 
I think I need to head out a little. 
...... 
They have begun to inject me with sedatives. 
...... 
I went looking for a former classmate. We grew up and studied together, and spent many years trying to one-up each other in our work and the impact factor of our research projects. He was shocked at the shallow and obvious nature of my question... I only asked him for his views on the Ætherside. Instead, he answered my question with another question: How do I regard the rising of the sun and the falling of the moon? Or the four seasons? I told him I am part of the seasonal cycle, and part of me rests in the rising sun and falling moon. 
He then called the police. The public safety officers of La Fantoma arrived quickly. 
...... 
I believe I have arrived at a UWST auto-farm. Convincing the ex-Oathkeeper security guard that I am not a Landbreaker in disguise proved quite a challenge. He shared some food and we sat before a stove, toasting with our good right hands. I asked him the same question. Fury, hatred, and a sprinkle of cowardice came to his eyes. He emptied his cup and then told me a story he heard when he was a boy. It was a tale about killing the ocean. 
The fire burned in his chest. I cannot let this fire harm you. Fortunately, I carried some sleeping pills with me. 
...... 
I can feel you very clearly now. 
...... 
The Archosauria woman sat within a formation of denstacks. Hah. She thinks her performance is impressive, but I saw right through her. I've used you to flip through numerous tomes to read about the conquerors and sovereigns whose names were noted down by history... I know the lies spat out by her kind of people. Listen to her voice, the empty shells of promises she sugarcoats. She treats the Ætherside as a tool... Of course, I might've been seeing things due to my extreme hunger. Anyway, if her theatrics and performance deceive me, then she's really good at what she's doing. 
...... 
I can wait no longer. I am going to find you. That Lei Fa thunder-casting Tianshi has not noticed me as I infiltrated the Exclusion Zone... I should be able to find a passage that leads to your location. 
...... 
The colors are so beautiful. I must enter it. It's time to go ... and become one with it.

Senior Staff Officer Master Gruman, I, Intel Officer Roland Arlos, hereby report the relevant details of this battle pursuant to the orders of Castellan Zasso. 
The battle was a 7-day engagement. We committed the 4th and 6th Standards comprising 22 banners and 6,143 combatants. Over 42,000 Aggeloid entities and 32 Ankhors were eliminated. Multiple unregistered Aggeloid construct patterns were sighted in this conflict, with average combat capabilities approaching or exceeding the Homoiossaron. Most samples have been sent to the Grand Archives for categorization. (COMMENT: Samples received. Though I appreciate having more intact samples, I am also aware that my inputs would hardly affect what I actually get.) 
The following is a summary of the actual battle events — 
INTERCEPTION: 
2300 hours, February 10, Year 152: Sector West-2 of the Aurora Belt picked up Ankhor-level readings. The 4th Standard was assembled according to the Order Codex for emergency airlift. 
0005 hours, February 11: Interception operation initiated. 
0008 hours, February 11: Ankhorfall occurred ahead of schedule and entered a mobile orbit. The interception fleet missed the estimated interception point and failed to inflict sufficient damage to most of the Ankhors. 
(COMMENT: The biggest and most severe failure of this entire battle. Why was the early warning facility located so far outside? If the Ankhors were targeting somewhere further back, perhaps we had already missed our window of early interception. Have the monitoring stations been redeployed to better locations?) 
CONTACT: 
0500 hours, February 11: Forward elements have established a line of defense at the plateau of battle sector M-320a, and commenced Aggeloid host extermination according to scout intel. Said elements then proceed to push toward known Ankhor sites. 
1100 hours, February 11: A new Ankhorfall barrage entered the field from low orbit height. Master Fintha responded and seized battle sectors M-322a and M-322b. A total of 4 assault banners (Gray Wedge, Flood Peak, Blazing Fire, and Black Wings) were committed as reinforcements to assault the Ankhorfall sites. 
(COMMENT: I must reiterate that issues stemming from our understrength field combat and early warning formations have become significant. Our assault banners should not be committed in such low-intensity conflicts. The Order is facing a worsening situation. We must introduce new detection measures, or train casters skilled in the Arts of detection and scrying and include them within our banners.) 
MAIN ENGAGEMENT: 
1600 hours, February 11: The battle escalated as the termination of the Ankhors occurred behind schedule. 
0100 hours, February 12: Sudden spike in Aggeloid spawning rates reported. Incoming bombardments forced us to retract the radius of anti-air coverage and impeded the transport of our reserves. Sightings of an unregistered Aggeloid pattern (temporarily codenamed "High Tower" by our frontline elements) were also confirmed. The assault banner Gray Wedge engaged the High Tower ahead of schedule, causing our frontal attack formations to disintegrate one after another. Contact with assault banners Flood Peak and Blazing Fire was lost. Preemptive tactical Ankhor strikes failed. Battlefield dynamics shifted to artillery duels and defense consolidation on both sides. 
1800 hours, February 13: Contact with assault banner Black Wings was lost. Battlefield dynamics have entered a complete stalemate. 
2100 hours, February 15: Numerous giant Aggeloi breached battle sector M-322a. Contact with assault banner Gray Wedge was lost. 
(COMMENT: We have an official codename for the unregistered Aggeloid pattern: Psithyrosson) 
ENDGAME: 
0800 hours, February 16: Mothership from the 6th Standard arrived at the field, providing the required reinforcements for securing air superiority. Effectiveness of our artillery formations was re-established. Master Grimnir deployed 15 banners of foot and artillery that successfully arrived in battle sector M-320a. 
2300 hours, February 18: All Ankhors eliminated. About 80% of the Aggeloi were neutralized. The remnants withdrew to the areas beyond the Aurora circle. Pursuit was no longer possible. 
For this battle, our two standards report a loss of 623 killed and 854 severely wounded. Our carrier mothership was forced to return to port for major repairs. Heavy losses were suffered by the foot banners Stone Claws, Weregild, and Thorned Razors. These banners have since been merged and re-organized. Assault banners Flood Peak, Blazing Fire, and Black Wings have been removed from our roster. One Oathkeeper, though no longer combat-capable, remains in the assault banner Gray Wedge. Pursuant to a signed directive from the Castellan, the understrength banner shall continue their crusade in our rear. 
(COMMENT: The Commandery has always respected the judgment of the frontlines. Nevertheless, the details of the concluding section were unnecessary. If you insist on defending that Oathkeeper of that assault banner, then I shall provide a more detailed analysis report regarding the Psithyrosson. Truth be told, I am not inclined to believe our best elites would commit an error as severe and inane as in this particular case. Also, given the limited intel we have so far, I have my doubts and suspicions about whether that entity can be classified as an Aggelos, if at all... In any case, I will do whatever is necessary, to the greatest extents permitted by our principles of justice and fairness.) 
This concludes our current understanding of the event. The Castellan awaits your reply. 

(COMMENT: My opinion has been furnished throughout this report. The original shall be mailed to you directly. Note that the Grand Archives is extremely concerned with the sudden pike in Aggeloid spawning rates. Your performances in this battle were less than ideal. Perhaps a face-to-face meeting can be arranged soon enough.)

Operator Chen Qianyu was a native of Hongshan City and once served at the Wuling Scientific Developmental District. Supervisor Perlica later recruited her, via a private channel, to Endfield Industries. She is now a core member of the Crisis Team. Given her outstanding capabilities and mobility, Operator Chen Qianyu is an indispensable component of the Team. 

Those seeking to join Endfield have demonstrated a wide range of literary skills when describing their motives. However, the HR Division has yet to establish basic standards for reviewing the [Personal Motivations] section. If this section were completed in a manner that is too curt and/or straightforward, I will ask the operator to re-write their motivations in a style that they are comfortable with. However, despite being given five standard days to revise this section, Operator Chen Qianyu still persisted in writing: "I just wanna join. It's fate." Reading this, I realized the need to reflect upon our current review standards and establish a new framework, while paying extra attention to the two blades that Operator Chen Qianyu placed on my table (though she claimed that she did not do so to threaten me). 
Operator Chen Qianyu's inner thoughts and feelings are not as casual as she makes them out to be. Taking into consideration of her relatively rich past experiences, it is obvious that the extremely brief and terse description of her personal motives was a conclusion she arrived at after an extended period of self-contemplation. 
Additionally, I also realized that Operator Chen Qianyu's recruitment has been specifically approved by Supervisor Perlica. From my readings, the recent years have been a period where our Supervisor exhibited emotional fluctuations. The operator managed to solve many potential issues by offering much needed stability and support. 
Most importantly, I may have neglected how the simple line: "I just wanna join. It's fate." is actually congruent to the inner logic of the Endfield strategic objectives. In other words, these words could be seen as an alternate interpretation of the "Unity in Purpose" approach in partnership espoused by our Endministrator, which I also have in my records. Perhaps we now have an explanation capable of satisfying all parties involved in this review. 
— Martin Marvin Malen, Assistant, HR Division, Endfield Industries

-5112800614410338075:
It was late at night. You saw smoke billowing from the next door workshop. The ringing of hammer striking the anvil could be heard within a three block radius. It was deliberate. It was loud.
"What is she trying to prove?" you didn't want to care, but suddenly remembered the maniac next door mumbling about the near-completion of her work. Thus, you turned around and headed next door while putting on your jacket, all the while mumbling this to yourself, "Talos forbid if she actually forges it."
Glowing embers floated through the gap of the workshop door. You now regret putting on the jacket as the place was terrifyingly hot. The light of the fire also lured in the tramp who lived three blocks away. She wore something cooler, and started scoffing at you right from the get-go.
"Idiot. Look at you, all bundled up. When was the last time you lit your smithy's furnace?" The tramp always talked like this since she could crawl. She envenomed her weapons with her spit.
You ignored her and pushed open the door. The entire house was awash by the fiery glow of the forge. The maniac stood besides it, and unleashed a hysterical riot of a laughter when she saw you two enter her workshop.
"You're too late! I shall be the one giving life to this weapon!" The maniac was wholly drenched in sweat. You saw only fanatical zealotry on her face.
The tramp got closer to the forge and studied the roiling hot ferrium. Her tone turned somber as she delivered these words: "This is bad. She's going to forge it."
Envy surged from your guts. You felt like vomiting.
You hated each other's guts, but the three of you were once the best of friends. You forgot how the hate actually started, or you grew up together. Even all those evenings you spent drinking together escaped your memories. The only thing you recalled was that prophecy spreading throughout Seš'qa: "A legendary weapon shall be born this winter. And only three smiths could hope to achieve this feat." As luck (or misfortune) would have it, the three of you happen to be the best smiths of the city.
Since then, all three of you became obsessed with forging the legendary weapon before the other two. Every meeting became a scheme and an attempt to beat the other senseless and throw them out of the city.
Both you and the tramp had nothing to say at this moment. A skilled smith need only look at the fire to know the immense power it held. The maniac worked the bellows to raise the furnace temperature, but try as she might, the furnace refused to get any hotter. She sighed and wiped away the sweat from her face.
The tramp's face darkened as she gloated: "You are going to fail."
The maniac, however, did not even bat an eye at you. She simply laughed: "Far from it!" And with that, she slit open her throat. Hot blood gushed out like lava and flowed into the furnace.
You and the tramp stretched out your hands together but it was too late. The maniac fell into the furnace and a deafening explosion echoed throughout the town. Fire spluttered out of the furnace chamber and spread throughout the entire workshop. The flames roared with greater fury and threatened to end the night itself. Even the skies feared what was about to happen, and desperately unloaded a great snow to put out the fire.
As the temperature continued its rapid rise, you looked at the tramp for a word. But decades of tacit understanding tell you that nothing needed to be said.
You approached the fire, ignored the painful burns, and worked the bellows once more. The nascent weapon within the forge hummed and complained. It was not hot enough. The temperature is too low. It demanded a flame with enough heat to sear a hole through the skies. The tramp sneered as you saw the blaze dancing in her eyes, a conflagration of fury, pain, regret, and ambition. Fire burst from her eyes and swallowed her whole. You had no time to grieve for the snowstorm of the night was relentless. It would do anything to put out their fires.
You were the idiot of the group who never mastered the Arts. The only recourse you had was better and more precise controls over the bellows for firing up the heat. Years of experience made you a master of keeping the fire going. The bellows swelled and emptied as the fire danced and howled. The flaming tongues licked your skin and it slowly gave way like molten wax. But the mere thought of the weapon maturing into its form gave you incredible elation and made you beam with satisfaction.
Did it hurt? It was far less painful than the last fight you had when the maniac tore a piece off your face with her teeth.
Before the flames completely devoured you, you finally remembered how they laughed with merriment back in the tavern.
The flames might not endure against the night-long blizzard, and there would be no trace of the three of you after the workshop fire. Nevertheless, you knew that a fireplace would remain, and within it they would find a sword capable of cleaving anything in the world apart.

As the great guns thundered into the skies, night finally returned to Fort Forgefane. The steam stopped hissing as the last Aggelos was crushed into gravel. Victory trumpeted throughout the icefields, the clarion call of triumph echoed amongst collapsed bastions before it reached a stone crypt used as a provisional morgue to house the fallen warriors.
To the smiths of Fort Forgefane, the clarion call felt more like a final farewell to the soldier. A forgesmith pulled a cart of salvaged equipment and paused before a young Oathkeeper, long bereft of breath.
Why did the smith stop? Was it his fear of death? He did not think so. He dreamed about falling like a true Oathkeeper soldier from the day he submitted his enlisting papers to the Order of Steel Oath. And since his first arrival at the gates of Fort Forgefane, he was determined to be a nail, permanently hammered into his post. There were only two things that could stop him from swinging his hammer: the future he dreamed had been achieved, or it became necessary for someone else to take his post.
The smith stooped over and took the long sword from the hands of the young soldier.
He could not remove his gaze from the soldier's face. Was he paying his final respects to a former comrade? No. He had said his farewells to all sorts of people in the south before he marched for the north. He saw his loved ones secretly weeping for his sake, witnessed the reluctance in their eyes, and even attended a close friend's funeral on the night before he reported to the training camp.
But what he felt at this very moment was new. A mysterious surge of emotions gripped him to the ground, even though he tried, again and again, to get himself to leave.
Heavy footsteps echoed in the crypt. The smith raised his head and held his breath.
"Lord Castellan Gerald! Apologies, I'm just ... salvaging the equipment."
The armored giant stretched out his hand and took the blade from the smith. The edge was curled and a fine crack ran along its length.
"Do you know him?"
"No... We're not familiar. But I did share some drink with him in the welcoming feast held for us several days ago..."
"What do you intend to do with this blade?"
The smith took the blade and shook off the snow from the hilt. He carefully studied the wounds suffered by the weapon and gave his verdict: "It will be my honor to return this blade to the furnace and have it recast, and the joy will be equal to seeing you throw this Aggeloid host back to whence they came. He is a hero ... that no one will remember."
"He is also a common man, just as common as this blade."
"My Lord Castellan... what would you have me do to this blade?"
"Even the perfect blade will one day shatter," Gerald patted the smith on the shoulder. "It shall be returned to the forge, pass through the ranks of Oathkeepers, and fulfill his unfinished duty."

Can you believe it, Lonna? I'm not on Talos-II when delivering this letter. 
You probably guessed it too. That's right! I was part of the special delegation from the Talos-II General Chamber of Commerce, and we were attending a closed-door meeting with Endfield aboard their ship, Dijiang. 
It was my first time boarding a vessel capable of traversing the sea of stars. And what a sea it is! It's far deeper and quieter than the oceans we have, with faint stars glittering in the distance. From space, Talos-II looks just like baby Baily fast asleep in his crib. 
Oh, my cute little Baily. Give our sweet baby a kiss on the head for me. 
I thought all my curiosities could be satisfied by the stars and the view of Talos-II from space, but on day four, Endfield arranged something special for us as part of the reception. We visited their zero gravity experience chamber. It looked like a simple, empty room. When we were ready, the lights grew dim and the sky window slowly opened, allowing the light from Talos the gas giant to pour in. The huge planet seized all of our attention. 
And then, gravity itself disappeared. 
Even for our negotiators and corporate officers. All of them lost their solemn gravity and instincts took over. My ears were filled with gasps of astonishment and wonder. I even heard a soft chuckle, and I swear it came from the Endfield operator who served as our guide. Looking at big-timer suits acting like playful or scared children must have offered a pure sense of joy. If this wasn't a closed-door and confidential meeting, the walls of this zero-g chamber would be plastered with photos of its "victims". 
As for me... I don't know how to say this to you, Lonna. When I floated in the sky, abandoned by every ounce of my weight and by the land itself, a refreshing sense of freedom coursed through my body as I faced the celestial object before me. I... 
I felt a sense of duty. 
A sense of the most impossible duty. 
I suddenly felt compelled to bring this experience to every resident of the Civilization Band. 
We are the children born into the cradle of Talosian gravity. But the birth of Dijiang would be the first time in our history when we finally have the chance to live differently. 
I remember father telling me that the most priceless thing is not a luxurious mansion or merchandise. That honor goes to the way of life. 
Can anything be more special than transcending the grips of gravity and living amongst the stars? 
We'll get an artificial geostationary orbit experience cabins in the future. We start from the basics, then work our way towards commercial complexes and space arenas. Every sport will get new rules, new tournaments, and new superstars competing in the zero-g environment. When knights wearing jet packs rocket through arenas, when race cars make perfect turns across toroid tracks, when the football flies into the goal under the influence of mechanics and gravity... When all these happen, our achievements will far outstrip any sum of money we imagined, Lonna. 
Of course, none of this would be possible without your support, dear. Do remember to take a look at the attached design drawings. Even if we didn't get the chance to pull it off, at least we can leave our ideas for posterity. If I secured your approval with proposal, then let us try to build this together and submit this to the concept design event. The company and the TGCC will remember it for us. 
I'll be back soon, but I really hope to hear back from you when I reach home, Lonna. 
Love you. 

NOTE: A design draft is attached to this letter. A table listing the manufacturing specifications is provided at the lower right corner of the draft. A temporary name has also been proposed: 
"Junction Point"

The YSTF has a secret chamber kept under tight security. They do not use it for storing intel files or documents, but for the "belongings" of every Yinglung. When you become an Yinglung, you are given a box and you are free to put anything you want in it. In the event that you fall during a mission, that thing in the box will function as the only proof of your existence. 
But Li Zhiyan's box remained empty. 
She told the chamber custodian that she had nothing. Everything she once had was buried within the dark, cold, and toxic Miasma of the North Wuling Exclusion Zone. 
The custodian had to tell her that this was a YSTF rule. It made Li think. What item best represents herself? If the title of YSTF Captain were taken from her, is there anything that she could put in the box? She pondered about the meaning of "self". 
She was only temporarily hampered by the question. Soon enough, she found an old artist on the market to write her name down with a calligraphy brush. This name was the thing that entered the box. 
The question did not feel important to her. It was the next mission that always mattered most. 
...... 
Li barely visited the secret chamber until recently. In her multiple visits, her once threadbare box began to fill. A pen. A button. A dagger also joined the pile... Every item appeared mundane and meaningless, as though she just grabbed something from the desk. A few seemed like gifts from her neighbors or keepsakes that someone wanted her to pass on... Yet Li treated them all like treasure and carefully placed them in her box. 
When a curious Endministrator asked about this, Li no longer responded with stern silence as she'd often done in the past. Instead, she gave a solemn answer. 
"I looked back and realized that I have missed so many things that I should have treasured."

DOCUMENT: Yvonne's work diary 
Day 3 after starting at that particular data section of the Æther rift. I can't see anything inside. All monitoring modules were knocked out. IR, EM, resonance responses — we got flatlined for everything. Not a single blip showed up. Sheesh. 
I tried to "read" the changes of that particular area with a smart sign language interpreter! And all I got was a bunch of errors and a single line that reads: "Failed to interpret data." 
We didn't just fail to monitor the stuff. The Æther rubbed it in our faces. We're completely blind to it. The only thing I'm certain of is this: It exists, and it's not very nice. 
I HATE THINGS I CAN'T SEE! 
............ 
Maybe I can change my approach. What would happen if I actively send data into it? Instead of just passively waiting for a response to come out of the output port, we should seize the initiative and interact with it instead. 
I tried three signal packs with different frequencies: (1) a standard greetings protocol; (2) a set of greetings I wrote myself in pulse-based format; (3) a set of static noise (the first note from the Movement: Genesis of the Universe, the Ætherside might like it). 
The results are just as predicted ... no responses. Fine. Be optimistic. Perhaps there was a response but receiving a radio wave transmission and emitting a response might take a while. If a single vibration takes at least 10 million years, then I have no choice but to keep Frost-e-Bytee on the receiving line. 
Perhaps I can try optical wave signals with various color codes. If that thing can see things, perhaps it'll like glittering stuff, like me! 
Plus light travels faster than sound! 
............ 
How many times did I fail again? Can't remember. Signal modulation, model simulations, and feedback monitoring ... none of it worked. The noise I'm getting sounds like the Æther laughing at me — I really hope it was laughing at me, because that means I'll unleash Frost-e-Bytee and ram some icy cold down its throat! 
I always believed that persistence will eventually identify a crack. But now I am beginning to wonder if this is a futile effort of exploration with no way out. 
We can't even "observe" this thing. How are we supposed to "decipher" it? 
The models I proposed and the devices I designed felt like childish gimmicks when compared to the Blight... 
............ 
Maybe the only thing I can do right now is to spin around on my swivel chair. Perhaps I gotta wait 10 million years for a miracle to happen. 
I might as well change my scientific approach. Time to build an invincible space armada. Let the ancient songs echo as I raise countless ... cities into the skies! Unfeasible? Maybe. But what can be more unfeasible than deciphering the Æther? 
I looked at those images of the Æther rift. I gazed at them long and hard. It devoured both sound and light. Even I got trapped within it — it crushed me and smothered me with eternal darkness. There is no escape for me. 
So why am I doing all this? To protect Talos-II...? To prove myself...? Because I got a grudge against Pa and Ma...? No. I think it all started on that day. I read about the Æther rift in the books and found it beautiful. So I snuck off to the Protection Band so I could observe it, like the giddy girl I was. The rift gave off a bright halo. Looking at it feels like staring straight into the sun. The piercing pain then gave way to a sense of indescribable horror and then it ... melted.

-4838437933790607992:
Camille always thought his emotions were well-hidden away. When compared to other operators who exercised zero restraints, he did a fine job. Unfortunately, unintended movements and barely noticeable body language still betrayed him. 
When frustrated, Camille would lower his gaze and study a crack, if any, on the ground, or subconsciously rub his shoulder blade. When he wishes to avoid contact, he would shift his center of balance to his right leg to expedite immediate flight. When hesitating or discomforted, his fingers would subconsciously rub the old, ancient key hanging from his waist. 
Many Endfield operators have an item or keepsake they focus on. For example, Yvonne treats Frost-e-Bytee as a close friend, Rossi has her dagger, and Da Pan is always carrying that ferrium wok on his back. But Camille is different. If anyone were to ask him about his key, he would immediately retract his hand as though the thing had become a burning brand. He would keep his lips tightly closed and refuse to respond to the inquiry. 
Skilled machinists would identify that the key was a handcrafted from something that resembled a music box cylinder, though Camille knows nothing about artisanry. The man has no property to his name, and no one knows what the key could actually open. 
Eventually, everyone became wiser and learned not to ask about the item. 
In the end, Camille confessed to the origins of the key during a casual conversation. It was a present personally crafted by his younger brother (the very same who broke all ties with him). It was part of their home at Seš'qa, which Camille later sold after an accident and no longer returned to. The key was merely ornamental and his habit of touching the key was rooted in longing ... and perhaps a dash of inexplicable ennui. After saying these words, Camille placed the key in one of his pockets. 
What he remembered was the searing pain as if a chunk of flesh were being torn from his body, and a dark and exhausting past that went on and on. The gift was offered when sincerity remained. The Keeper faced a dilemma, and he no longer wanted to be reminded. 
A few days later, Camille received a Baker toast and visited the Endministrator's office. He was received by a smiling Endministrator who dropped a new key into his hands. 
"Such keys and locks are pretty rare, so making them took quite a while," the person said, "I just want you to know that Dijiang always has a door that you can open." 
It caught Camille by surprise. He tightly wrapped his fingers around the key and turned his face aside. He tried to form words, but they came out like noises made by a wheezing fowl whose neck was caught in an iron grip. In the end, he only managed to blurt out a barely audible phrase: "Thank you." 
Not everybody is familiar with Camille's body language, but everyone knows that the jingling of the new key against the old is joyous, like how he felt at that very moment.

I met them in the wilderness.
They were not friendly at first. One of their Aldertones inspected my wounds and permitted me to stay until I became well enough to move on my own. The others, however, refused to converse with me. Perhaps this was the price that I had to pay for wearing a uniform of TGCC origin.
Their way of life left quite ... an impression on me. These people developed a unique culture centered around the idea of "simplicity". No. "Restraint" would be a better word. They might not have the best technology, but they made the most out of every material. These people crafted tools with a unique minimalist aesthetic — a style of beauty molded by the harsh and unforgiving wildlands of this untamed world.
I told them I was a crafter and it gave me a chance to take part in their work. Observing their craftsmanship up close gave me a rather shocking revelation — their weapons were fashioned using far less materials and simpler processes, but overall performance was only marginally less than our TGCC counterparts. This discovery made me realize that our designs actually have plenty of room for improvement.
I left the Circuit after spending three whole years with them, and they gave me honors befitting their own Aldertones. Deep down, I learned far more from the people of the Circuit than what I taught them in return.

She would arrive at the cemetery to pray in the morning and leave at noon. Then she would do some community work in the afternoon, return to the cemetery during the evening, and leave the place only in the deep of night. I followed her before. Her home was no more than a klick southeast of the cemetery. Like most Songseekers of the Hannabit Circuit, she could survive the wildlands on her own.
She did not avoid external contact. Some of the UWST crew mates talked to her before to barter a thing or two.
She appeared young, gentle, and even a little shy. There was nothing dangerous about her.
But you must know the closest Circuit settlement was over a hundred klicks away. We have but only 1 cemetery at this place and only one undertaker!
I did my own investigations. The people we buried here had nothing to do with her. Most were travelers killed by the Aggeloi or Blight accidents. With the exception of the unmarked headstones, I checked all the names and every one of them went missing in recent years.
It got me spooked. In fact, even the truckers and crew mates driving past this place were getting spooked.
I'm quitting. I'll do this just for another week and I'll give you all the photos and video recordings I've made. I don't care about the money. I'm getting my sorry arse out of this blighted place.

-4705231213366901567:
Not everyone's heart was mine to touch, but I could read my own like a book.
In this very instant, my heart is filled with nothing but fear. Our science station, the "observatory" we constructed to defeat the boundless Very Large Rift, has been engulfed by the Blight and despair did likewise to my mind. Will the Xiranite succeed? Is the entirety of our efforts completely meaningless? The Æther made us realize how insignificant we are. It will devour Wuling and everything in existence. How are we supposed to oppose this astronomical phenomenon?
......
A canal must be constructed. Although rescue work of victims from the disaster site is top priority right now, this canal is of utmost necessity. It will prevent the aquifers from contamination by the Blight Tide seeping into the soil. But this is ultimately futile. It only delays the inevitable death of everything upon this land.
......
My hands are covered in blisters. Though I'm just a worker at the production floor with zero knowledge on construction, I have been assigned to a building crew... We must fight off the disaster until reinforcements arrive from our HQ.
......
I got a cut in my hand. I unearthed a broken dagger from the canal construction site. How long has it been buried here? A century? By Talos, take a good look at your bleeding hand! To hell with glory and sacrifice! Why am I still alive? Why do I want to be alive? Why should I be alive at all? WHY?
......
Blighted hell. I'll off myself tomorrow.
......
I chose the night. At the construction site. Good place. Perfect weather, with pouring rain that soaks everything in the friggin' mud. Losers like us deserve to die and get buried in the mud.
The rain-swollen torrents tore through the last unfinished section of the canal. I spotted a metallic sheen in the freshly exposed mud. I don't know why I walked over to the glint and scooped out the mud with my bare hands. I unearthed the thing buried beneath — a rusty valve.
That was it.
Ours was an ad-hoc rush job with neither infrastructure map data nor verification. And as chance would have it, we completed the canal that our predecessors failed to finish.
My view of the thoroughly rusted valve transformed at once. It was my father's will, my mother's portrait, the paper flowers offered to my grandparents' grave...
...and me... I saw my reflection in the muddy water.
That was it.
Someone always wanted to survive. And someone always survived.
The heavens and earth are not without boundaries. Fear itself could disintegrate completely.
With that, I stopped thinking about death.
I but extend the facet of survival and persistence, the never-ending cycle that has endured for since time immemorial.

Operator Da Pan (ID name: Pan Yuan) is a member of the Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS). He claims to be a very well-traveled chef and trader. He has joined the Specialist Tech Division as an independent, with recommendations from Operator Chen Qianyu and a letter of authentication from HAS. We also respected his personal wishes and granted him partial authority levels for canteen access. 

Da Pan provided an incredibly chaotic CV. His verifiable work experiences include: owner of hot pot eatery, LA-ME-DA (literal translation: Spicily Huge); tianshi at HAS; electrician; carpenter; machinist; and background extra in Heyi Quan: Zailin (literal translation: Fist of Combined Will: Revisited). 
Two of his past experiences cannot be verified. The first was a brief stint of driving taxis at Simonch. We failed to find any commercial driving license or records for Da Pan in the said city. When I pointed out this finding, the Ursus' maw cracked into a 70-degree smile and he applied a rather powerful slap on my mechanical chassis. The second would be "friendly assists and support". Da Pan claims he part-timed as an ornamental burdenbeast stand-in for three days at La Fantoma. By the time I realized that I had been misled into an engrossing dialog about unlicensed taxi driving and ornamental burdenbeasts, we had already been talking for four hours — and I had neglected to ask Da Pan about the experiences that he should remember best: his time as a tianshi at HAS. 
While verifying his experiences in HAS, Da Pan became visibly downcast and displeased. But he quickly resumed his smile and deflected the topic with a casual joke. Then he showed me a friendly group photo of him and other ornamental burdenbeasts. I could obviously tell that he was trying to avoid talking about his disagreeable past with other Tianshi, but this is not a negative consideration for Endfield. Since Da Pan is still affected by the Science Station incident, it proves that he remains, deep inside, a HAS tianshi who upholds a strong sense of principles, responsibilities, and duty. 
— Martin Marvin Malen, Assistant, HR Division, Endfield Industries

-4297975222758153993:
After the fall of Sami, most of the Sami people accepted the outcome. They live atop the Feranmut's remains, carrying on His will, fighting the Aggelos to protect Talos-II.
Yet there were still Snowpriests who believed that Sami had not truly died. His soul had merely been lost within the rifts, fallen into a deep slumber. One day, Sami would wake from His dream and return to His people. They traveled to the rifts across Talos-II, setting up altars and performing rituals, trying to call Sami's soul back from the fissures. But none who went ever returned. Later, with the northern front growing ever more urgent, no one was willing to continue the attempt.
In a snowy forest near the Wuling Very Large Rift, Typhoeus found the manuscripts left behind by one of those Sami Snowpriests. The manuscripts detailed all her attempts to awaken Sami. Though Typhoeus was able to confirm through her own exploration that the ritual had failed and the Snowpriestess had vanished without a trace, the girl still caught a faint whiff of possibility from the remaining materials.
Unfortunately, after months of study, Typhoeus had made no progress.
She asked every Snowpriest and shaman in the Order of Steel Oath and Myrkwood, but they all just shook their heads, believing it to be a doomed endeavor.
Even after hitting so many dead ends, Typhoeus did not lose heart. The Snowpriestess's unique insights on dreams in the manuscripts taught the girl to perceive special revelations within the dreamscapes of others.

"I don't know why, but lately I keep dreaming of being chased by a gigantic monster. The ground beneath my feet keeps swaying, as if I am standing on a suspension bridge. I toss and turn all night long..."
"Simple. That monster is hunting you, and you have been cornered."
"What should I do?"
"Become stronger. Do not be the prey. Be the hunter instead."
"I think I get it now."

After that conversation with Typhoeus, the operator mapped out a full month of intensive training for himself. The exhaustion and sense of accomplishment from the workouts let him sleep soundly through the night. Before long, Endfield colleagues began showing up at Typhoeus's door with all sorts of dreams, asking her to read and interpret them.
And Typhoeus, after listening to everyone's dreams, drew inspiration from them to craft a legend of her own, one that wove together the Feranmut Sami, dreams, and the Snowpriests.
Soon, Typhoeus finished writing the ending. She thought the matter would settle just like the story itself. So she gathered her notes and set off to share the conclusion with those who had been waiting eagerly. But halfway there, she brushed past a young girl in the corridor.
Typhoeus did not recognize her, yet she felt a strangely familiar presence emanating from her.
It was a presence that had accompanied her people through swamps and forests, through winters and into springs, from birth all the way to death.
By the time Typhoeus came to her senses, the girl had already walked far away.
Later, she learned from others the girl's codename: Last Rite.
Driven by a mysterious premonition, she tore out the ending she had written and wrote that codename on a fresh page instead.

DOCUMENT: A certain log that requires sufficient authority level 
According to reports by members of Operations Team Z7, Antal is exceptionally skilled in Originium Arts. His ability to cast the Arts far exceeds that of other operators in his cohort. When conducting a certain operation, Op Team Z7 members witnessed how Antal, in a crucial moment, positioned himself before the hostage. The operator used his Originium Arts to instantly disintegrate the greatsword swung by the attacking Landbreaker, and saved both himself and the hostage. 
It was an extremely intense moment. Antal would immediately lose his life if he failed to de-weaponize the attacker. However, he himself remained extremely calm throughout the entire incident. Since then, members of Op Team Z7 gained a deeper appreciation of Antal's abilities — Though he was known for being slow when it comes to sensing dangers in the environment or picking up changes in the emotions of other people, he was willing to risk his own life to save others. This revealed Operator Antal to be an extremely kind and courageous individual. 
Antal was remarkably humble when his teammates asked him about what he did. Antal replied that he did not perfectly wield his Originium Arts and failed to achieve his grandmother's level of expertise. He claimed the old lady could take apart and reassemble large metal machinery, while disintegrating a Landbreaker's weapon was the most he could do. Antal also mentioned that his grandmother crafted a small staff for him during his childhood to make up for his lack of power. 
"Your talent lies elsewhere — That is what my grandmother told me. And I have absolutely faith in her words."

[AUDIO LOG EXCERPT 1]
"AHEM— Talosian Calendar Year 15, ██ of ██. Day three after moving into the temporary shelters... QUIET, TORY! You're supposed to fix the chair, not bring down the house!
"Quit nagging already. And enough yapping about your fine studio at downtown Wrankwood. Hell, even I like a hot water bath and trashy movies to go along with it. But clean towels are a luxury now, okay?
"Oh, why don't you heard north, find 'Mr. Angels', take him out for a drink, and ask where his blighted kind hid the keys to the Cosmic Gate? —OF COURSE I KNOW IT DOESN'T EXIST. Where did your sense of humor go? Blown to pieces along with the stabilizer and the blighted Aggeloi?
"What am I doing? I'm making an audio log. Say, how about lending me that camcorder of yours? Your documentary project is on a temporary hold, right...? No? Fine. Blighted camera crew and their pride.
"Where was I again? Oh, yes. Today is Talosian Calendar Year 15—"

[AUDIO LOG EXCERPT 2]
"Dallied around for two weeks and still no news about the others. Murray, Ellie, Henry... I think they're still alive. I gotta keep thinking positive.
"We're one of the lucky ones. At least we got a roof here. The other shelters are jam-packed of people. They told me the war is over but there's no heading back to Terra. Meals are getting worse, too. Sheesh...
"...You're back? Wait. What the hell is that? A sword? You traded a can-o-food for a friggin' razor?! Are you friggin' nuts...?! Oh yeah, great! It killed a buggerloid! So what? Your backup camera almost got one of those buggers too —— KYAA! STOP! I'm sorry! It was my fault!
"You heard Ellie and Murray ended up at the shelters organized by the United Workers' HQ? Awesome. But I heard they have some serious hunger games going on at that place. I heard the UW is meeting up with the Corporate Security Council to talk about some 'shelter program'. Hah. This reminds me of the friggin' boring news on Terra. Never thought I would actually start reading these articles.
"Just ... try to stay here, Tory. Enough scavenging and trading already. Save your pitiful rations.
"And try to check your camcorder... Why? I don't know. I just ... just kinda feel we might get to use it again."

[AUDIO LOG EXCERPT III]
"Hmm... how long has it been? I hardly kept count. Maybe more than five months, maybe?
"Tory and I are now part of the Corporate Security Council entourage — Temporary, of course. We just tag along for a chance to get some worthy footage.
"So this entourage just got demolished yesterday. While beating the retreat, they ran into another equally ragtag band. Turned out to be peeps from the UW.
